question_text: A 26-year-old woman presents to her physician at the 3rd week postpartum with a fever and a swollen breast with redness and tenderness. She has been breastfeeding her infant since birth. The symptoms of the patient started 4 days ago. She has not taken any antibiotics for the past 12 months. She does not have any concurrent diseases. The vital signs include: blood pressure 110/80 mm Hg, heart rate 91/min, respiratory rate 15/min, and temperature 38.8℃ (101.8℉). Physical examination reveals redness and enlargement of the right breast. The breast is warm and is painful at palpation. There is purulent discharge from the nipple. No fluctuation is noted. Which of the following is a correct management strategy for this patient?

        ### Question
        A 26-year-old woman presents to her physician at the 3rd week postpartum with a fever and a swollen breast with redness and tenderness. She has been breastfeeding her infant since birth. The symptoms of the patient started 4 days ago. She has not taken any antibiotics for the past 12 months. She does not have any concurrent diseases. The vital signs include: blood pressure 110/80 mm Hg, heart rate 91/min, respiratory rate 15/min, and temperature 38.8℃ (101.8℉). Physical examination reveals redness and enlargement of the right breast. The breast is warm and is painful at palpation. There is purulent discharge from the nipple. No fluctuation is noted. Which of the following is a correct management strategy for this patient?

        ### Options

opb. Prescribe dicloxacillin and bromocriptine for halting lactation
opc. Manage with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and encourage continuing breastfeeding
opd. Prescribe trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and recommend emptying affected breast without feeding
ope. Manage with clindamycin and recommend to interrupt breastfeeding until the resolution
